part_C_q9_argmin.note: which elementary symmetric function attains the minimum valuation, per section, against the depth

theorem: v_lambda(e_k(D)) >= 2k for every 1 <= k <= q-1, q an odd prime.  Proof: p_1 = tr D = 0, so Newton reads k e_k = sum_{i>=2} (-1)^{i-1} e_{k-i} p_i; with v(p_i) >= v(q)+i and induction v(e_{k-i}) >= 2(k-i), each term has valuation >= 2k - i + v(q) >= 2k because i <= k <= q-1 = v(q); and k is a lambda-unit.  This is precisely the Pass-485 eigenvalue conjecture for every elementary symmetric function except the top one, so the entire residual gap in the unified determinant law is now the single coefficient e_q = det D.  The induction breaks at k=q because there i can equal q and the constraint i <= v(q) = q-1 fails by exactly one.
